summary: Tested the new menu/pages editor feature end-to-end (backend + frontend). Backend: 7/7 pytest tests pass covering public GET /api/menu defaults, admin direct update with persistence + bare-domain auto-https prefix, 25-item cap, pages dict sanitized to {squads,notices,register}, empty-label 422 validation, editor PUT → pending change with public menu unchanged → admin approval reflects publicly, and unauthenticated 401/403. Frontend: Admin Menus tab renders with all required testids; toggling the Squads page off makes nav-link-squads and footer-link-squads disappear and /squads shows the page-unavailable screen with Back-to-home link; toggling Register CTA off hides nav-register-cta; adding a new 'Notices' item appears in both navbar and Explore footer; up-arrow reorder reflects on the live site; client-side 'Give every menu item a name before saving' validation blocks url-without-label; Reset to defaults restores the 4 original items. Editor flow: editor sees Menus tab, save shows 'Submitted — an admin must approve it before it goes live', public /api/menu unaffected until admin approves/rejects via Approvals tab. Regression: all 10 admin tabs (Registrations, Messages, Announcements, Squads, Pop-up, Homepage, Menus, Security, Approvals, Users) render; public routes /, /squads, /notices, /register return 200; footer 'Designed by Iravati Solutions' credit intact. STATE RESTORED: public /api/menu back to 4 default items, all 3 pages ON, Register CTA ON, pending editor change rejected.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: _clean_menu reassigns a fresh uuid to every item on every save, so item IDs are not stable across edits — fine today because the frontend doesn't rely on them, but if the UI ever needs stable per-item keys (e.g. per-item approval diffs or analytics), consider preserving the incoming id when valid.

Minor: PUT /api/admin/menu has no explicit role check for 'admin' or 'editor' — any authenticated user with a valid token can either save directly (admin) or queue a pending change. If there are/will be other authenticated roles (e.g. viewer), add an allow-list; today only admin/editor exist, so this is latent risk, not a bug.
Non-blocking: server.py is 1495 lines — consider splitting menu/pages, popup, homepage, and auth into separate routers for maintainability (threshold in review guidelines is 700).
seed_data_creation: None added. Pending editor change created during tests was rejected; menu returned to defaults.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Menu feature is fully working. /app/backend/tests/test_menu.py uses pytest fixtures that reset menu to defaults before AND after every test and rejects any lingering menu pending changes, so it's safe to re-run. Testids reference: admin tab triggers use text (page.get_by_role('button', name='Menus')), the inner MenuTab container has data-testid='menu-tab', the Approvals tab shows the pending menu change under resource='menu' with description 'Menu & pages update'.
